citations.passage:
IIIF gives archival viewers standardized deep-zoom image serving plus
manifests that carry page order and metadata; adopting it means a client's
scans stay portable across viewer implementations instead of locked to a
custom gallery.

Fifteen Dublin Core elements cover the descriptive fields the archive needs
— title, creator, date, subject, rights — without a bespoke schema; Quill &
Marrow drafted the house style on top of them for the Larkspur metadata.

judge.rationale: The answer correctly identifies decision d-011, the iiif-overview reading notes, and their relationship to the archive-metadata notes and Larkspur’s Dublin Core house style. However, it omits the notes’ portability-across-viewers rationale, Quill & Marrow’s role, and the fact that the house style was based on fifteen Dublin Core elements, while adding the more specific claim that IIIF manifests transport that Dublin Core metadata.
